pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered as optimisation rather than instruction, given he already trains six to seven times a week - 'the main thing would be optimizing the way that you're doing the workouts right now' - and answered with a flat 'yes'. No questions and no elaboration.

The pillar he had actually asked for. He raised it himself in discovery ('I don't want to count calories. And right now, I kind of count calories') and the rep tied the when-what-how-much frame to it and to his carnivore question. Reaction on delivery was a single 'Yeah.'

The only pillar that drew a real reaction, and it is the one he is buying: 'Yeah, yeah, that's what I'm looking for right there', in response to the teach-you-everything-so-you-can-continue-yourself framing plus direct access to Trevor's cell number.

anchors.raw: we can do one month first. That's 1,200 a month. Then if we split it up into six, it would be 1,200 a month, but we can do one month.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor and Primal set it. The moment a $1,200 single month existed, the $6,000 six months stopped being the decision on the table. The rep then named and immediately talked down a $4,000 three-month tier as well, leaving the cheapest option as the recommendation.

anchors.raw: my social media right now is like doing really well with like my fitness stuff. So I'm kind of wanting to maybe entertaining the aspect of like, maybe like coaching online or selling programs
anchors.note: The strongest supporting anchor available and it was never used. He is buying an input to a business he intends to build - 'I have countless people asking me for kettlebell like programs' - which makes this a professional investment rather than a personal expense. Nobody priced it that way.

anchors.raw: I watch all his YouTube videos. I kind of really like the direction he has and the mindset that he has.
anchors.note: Fourth appearance in this batch of Primal's free content as the prospect's existing solution. Here it converted, but it also fed the eight-weeks argument: someone who has already absorbed the free library reasonably believes he needs less than six months.

unmet_demand.want: To learn Trevor's methodology in order to coach others and sell his own programmes online - he said so twice, unprompted and in detail
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nobody addressed it. There is no stated position on whether clients may resell or teach the methodology, no licensing or certification path, and no IP conversation. A prospect openly buying to build a coaching business in the same niche was sold a one-month tier and told he would learn everything and could 'pass it on to other people'.

unmet_demand.want: A short, intensive knowledge transfer - 'what might take someone six months I can get done in a month'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is built and priced as six months. Rather than defending why, the rep created a one-month version on the call, which means the demand was met by improvisation rather than by product. If experienced prospects routinely want a condensed version, that is a real product question rather than a one-off concession.

unmet_demand.want: Guidance on whether carnivore is appropriate for him, which he raised specifically
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered only with a promise that Trevor is knowledgeable and would look at it. Not a gap in the offer so much as a question deferred, recorded because it was one of only two substantive product questions he asked.
